title: Ozempic and Wegovy May Slow Biological Aging
hook: Semaglutide, the drug behind Ozempic and Wegovy, slowed biological aging markers in a study of adults with HIV — the first clinical evidence it may affect aging itself, not just weight or blood sugar.
key_points: Researchers studied semaglutide's effect on biological aging markers in adults with HIV.
The drug slowed those aging markers — the first clinical evidence of this effect.
This is a new angle beyond semaglutide's known uses for diabetes and weight loss.
Scientists say larger studies are needed before concluding it can slow aging generally.
content_html: Semaglutide — the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy — is already known for lowering blood sugar and driving weight loss. A new study adds an unexpected angle: it may also slow biological aging.
extra_html:
As ScienceDaily reports, researchers tracked markers of biological aging in adults with HIV who took semaglutide and found the drug slowed those markers — the first clinical evidence that a GLP-1 medication may influence aging itself, rather than just the metabolic conditions it's already prescribed for.

The finding joins a growing list of effects researchers are uncovering for GLP-1 drugs well beyond their original purpose. But this is early-stage evidence in a specific population, and scientists caution that larger, broader studies are needed before concluding semaglutide can meaningfully slow aging for people in general. For now, it's a promising research lead rather than a reason to take the drug for anything other than what it's approved for.

related.title: Why GLP-1 Drugs Don't Work for Everyone
related.hook: Scientists found genetic variants — carried by roughly 1 in 10 people — that seem to cause a kind of 'GLP-1 resistance,' making drugs like Ozempic less effective at controlling blood sugar.

related.title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Lower Breast Cancer Risk
related.hook: A large study found women on GLP-1 drugs were about 30% less likely to develop breast cancer — a promising association, not yet proof, with trials now being planned to test it.

related.title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Lower Addiction Risk
related.hook: A study of ~600,000 U.S. veterans links GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide to lower rates of addiction and overdose — an association, not proof that the drugs cause the effect.

flashcards.back_html: It slowed markers of biological aging in adults with HIV — the first clinical evidence that the drug may influence aging itself, not just weight or blood sugar.

flashcards.prompt: How confident should we be that semaglutide slows aging in general?

choices.text: Not very yet — larger studies are needed before drawing that conclusion
Completely confident — this is settled, proven science
It's already an approved anti-aging treatment

flashcards.explanation_html: This is early clinical evidence in a specific population (adults with HIV). Researchers say larger studies are needed before concluding semaglutide slows aging more broadly.
